race.name: Dirty Sheets Gravel Grind
race.tagline: One hundred miles of punchy Georgia gravel, pavement, and singletrack outside Atlanta.

vitals.field_size: 200-rider limit for the 100-mile race; 600 riders across all distances
vitals.registration: BikeReg; 2026 entry ranges from $85 early to $150 day-of if space remains
vitals.prize_purse: $3,000 split equally between the 100-mile men's and women's fields
vitals.aid_stations: Multiple well-stocked aid stops plus roaming SAG support
vitals.cutoff_time: 6:00 PM estimated course completion at a 10 mph average

climate.description: Mid-October conditions can swing from cool and wet to warm and dusty; humidity and recent rain materially change the unpaved and trail sections.

terrain.surface: The organizer publishes a 52/48 gravel-to-pavement split with rolling backroads plus purpose-built singletrack and doubletrack around Serenbe and Moore's Bridge.

gravel_god_rating.score_note: A 100-mile, 6,815-foot mixed-surface race with real trail sections, full support, prize money, and an organizer-built weekend; regional prestige and field depth keep it in Tier 3.

biased_opinion.summary: Dirty Sheets is no generic local gravel loop: the 2026 flagship stacks 100+ miles, 6,815 feet, pavement, gravel, singletrack, and doubletrack into an unmarked course. Full SAG, aid stops, prize money, hand-made trophies, camping, and a complete weekend lift the experience; regional prestige and field depth keep it in Tier 3.
strengths: Real surface variety, including singletrack and doubletrack
Full SAG and well-stocked aid stops
$3,000 equal prize purse and hand-made trophies
weaknesses: Regional rather than national field depth
Unmarked course demands reliable GPS navigation
Tentative route can change before race day
Variable fall weather can transform the trail sections
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A serious hundred-mile mixed-surface race hiding in Atlanta's backyard. Travel for the course and community, not for a nationally stacked field.

final_verdict.one_liner: One hundred miles of punchy Georgia gravel, pavement, and singletrack outside Atlanta.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a fully supported, legitimately hard Southeast mixed-surface race without the destination-race circus; no if national field depth is the main attraction.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a bigger national field, choose Gravel Worlds. For another rugged Southeast challenge, compare Pisgah Monster-Cross or Hot Springs Gravel Gauntlet.

logistics.airport: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), approximately 30 miles from Serenbe
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in or near Serenbe for the shortest race-morning transfer; broader south-Atlanta lodging is available around the airport and Newnan.
logistics.food: Bring race nutrition to Chattahoochee Hills; registration includes post-race food and drinks.
logistics.packet_pickup: Thursday evening in College Park, Friday evening at MTB Atlanta HQ, or race morning in Serenbe
logistics.parking: Organizer-directed field parking at Serenbe Flower Meadows, 10690 Hutchesons Ferry Road
logistics.camping: Tent and RV camping is available at MTB Atlanta HQ for the 2026 race weekend

eligibility.status_note: The organizer confirms the timed 100-mile race for Saturday, October 17, 2026, with category starts, podiums, prize money, and open BikeReg registration.

history.founder: MTB Atlanta / North Georgia Mountain Bike Association
history.origin_story: The event turns the gravel backroads known locally as Dirty Sheets into a supported race weekend that funds regional trail building and maintenance.
notable_moments: The 2026 flagship course adds Moore's Bridge and Serenbe singletrack and doubletrack to the established mixed-surface loop.
history.reputation: A community-built Atlanta-area gravel race known for punchy terrain, hand-made trophies, and an unusually complete race-weekend experience.

course_description.character: A punchy 100-mile mixed-surface course with 6,815 feet of repeated climbing, moving among pavement, gravel, singletrack, and doubletrack.

suffering_zones.desc: The repeated punchy climbs and changing surfaces begin to compound near the middle of the hundred-mile course.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Repeated rolling climbs on mixed surfaces

suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Punchy climbing with gravel and trail sectors

course_description.signature_challenge: Holding power and handling together across 100 miles, 6,815 feet of repeated climbing, four surface types, and an unmarked GPS course.

guide_variables.race_terrain: 52% gravel, 48% pavement, plus singletrack and doubletrack
race_challenges: Surface changes between pavement, gravel, singletrack, and doubletrack
GPS navigation on an unmarked course

non_negotiables.why: The flagship course combines 100+ miles, 6,815 feet of climbing, and repeated surface changes.
The organizer does not mark the course and requires riders to use GPS files across gravel, pavement, and trail sections.

non_negotiables.requirement: Race fueling at a ten-hour pace
non_negotiables.why: The organizer's completion target assumes a 10 mph average through 6:00 PM; fueling must survive a full day rather than only the fast opening miles.

topics.pacing: Pacing 6,815 feet of repeated climbing without over-riding the opening pavement
topics.navigation: Racing an unmarked GPS course without missed turns
topics.surface_transitions: Handling pavement, loose gravel, singletrack, and doubletrack efficiently

marketplace_variables.race_hook: One hundred miles of punchy Georgia gravel, pavement, and singletrack outside Atlanta.
marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: 6,815 feet of climbing, an unmarked GPS course, and repeated surface changes punish anyone who treats the opening miles like a road race.

logistics.explanation: The Serenbe start is roughly 30 miles from Atlanta's airport, with three packet-pickup windows, organizer-directed parking, camping, and clear start waves. Field parking and a rural start keep it below turnkey destination-race logistics.

length.explanation: The organizer's flagship is 100+ miles with an estimated 6:00 PM completion at a 10 mph average. That is a full endurance race, with 62- and 22-mile options preserving accessibility without diluting the main event.

technicality.explanation: The 52/48 gravel-pavement split understates the handling demand: the 2026 route adds purpose-built singletrack and doubletrack, rough patches, and unmarked GPS navigation. It rewards control and equipment judgment without becoming a mountain-bike race.

elevation.explanation: The official 100-mile page lists 6,815 feet of climbing. There is no single marquee ascent; repeated punchy Chattahoochee Hills climbs accumulate fatigue across the entire course.

climate.explanation: A mid-October Georgia start usually avoids peak summer heat, but a long day can still move from a cool morning to a warm, humid afternoon. Rain changes the gravel and trail sectors far more than the paved mileage.

altitude.explanation: Chattahoochee Hills sits barely above sea level in gravel terms. Zero altitude consideration needed for preparation or performance. If you're coming from elevation, expect to feel stronger; if you're from sea level, this changes nothing. Lower altitude than Gravel Worlds — no thin-air concerns.

adventure.explanation: The course escapes metro Atlanta into rural Chattahoochee Hills, then mixes backroads with wooded singletrack and doubletrack. GPS-only navigation and the surface variety give it more adventure than a standard supported fondo.

prestige.explanation: 2024 results show Brock Mason winning the 102-mile in 4:52:50, with 16th place Logan Hunt finishing in 7:45:23—a nearly three-hour spread indicating regional competition rather than elite depth. The $3,000 prize purse split between men and women suggests ambition exceeding current field strength.

race_quality.explanation: Category waves, timing hardware, cash payouts, full SAG, stocked aid stops, professional media, and distance-specific field limits form a credible race operation. The route remains tentative and unmarked, which caps the score.

experience.explanation: Camping, two pre-race pickup parties, a shakeout ride, post-race food and drinks, live entertainment, free photos, and a Sunday coffee ride make this a real weekend rather than a number pickup and finish-line banana.

community.explanation: All profits support MTB Atlanta trail building and maintenance, and the organizer uses locally built trail sectors and hand-thrown Georgia trophies. The race directly reinvests participation into the terrain riders use.

field_depth.explanation: Times span from Jason Thomas's 1h 23m effort to Mary Hawthorne's 4h 31m recreational ride, showing wide participation but limited elite depth. The 2024 men's field stretched over nearly three hours from winner to mid-pack, suggesting strong regional participation without national competitive draw. Less competitive depth than Almanzo 100.

value.explanation: Entry starts at $85 and includes full support, aid, a rider shirt, food, drinks, entertainment, photos, and a raffle; proceeds support trail work. Late pricing rises sharply, so value depends on registering early.

expenses.explanation: Proximity to Atlanta keeps flights and lodging competitive, while onsite camping can replace a hotel. A car is still the practical way to reach Serenbe, and day-of registration can reach $150.

rider_intel.search_text: The Dirty Sheets Gravel Grind in Chattahoochee Hills features a mix of terrain that riders describe as challenging but not overly difficult. The course includes a technical single track section and steep, short punchy climbs through chunky rough terrain. These climbs are particularly notable because success depends heavily on line selection - riders who pick good lines can power through, while others may need to walk. The route covers approximately 20 miles around the Chattahoochee Hills area near Atlanta. Riders emphasize that while the course has challenging sections, it remains accessible to a range of skill levels, making it a popular choice for group rides and social events in the gravel cycling community.
